### Go Ethereum vulnerable to DoS via malicious p2p message
[CVE-2025-24883](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-24883) / [GHSA-q26p-9cq4-7fc2](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-q26p-9cq4-7fc2)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

A vulnerable node can be forced to shutdown/crash using a specially crafted message.

During the peer-to-peer connection handshake, a shared secret key is computed. The implementation
did not verify whether the EC public key provided by the remote party is a valid point on the secp256k1 curve.
By simply sending an all-zero public key, a crash could be induced due to unexpected results from the handshake.

The issue was fixed by adding a curve point validity check in https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/commit/159fb1a1db551c544978dc16a5568a4730b4abf3

##### Patches

A fix has been included in geth version 1.14.13 and onwards.

##### Workarounds

Unfortunately, no workaround is available.

##### Credits

This issue was originally reported to Polygon Security by David Matosse (@​iam-ned).

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.6 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:U`

### go-ethereum vulnerable to DoS via malicious p2p message
[CVE-2024-32972](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-32972) / [GHSA-4xc9-8hmq-j652](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-4xc9-8hmq-j652) / [GO-2024-2819](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2024-2819)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

A vulnerable node can be made to consume very large amounts of memory when handling specially crafted p2p messages sent from an attacker node.

In order to carry out the attack, the attacker establishes a peer connections to the victim, and sends a malicious `GetBlockHeadersRequest` message with a `count` of  `0`, using the `ETH` protocol. 

In `descendants := chain.GetHeadersFrom(num+count-1, count-1)`, the value of `count-1` is passed to the function `GetHeadersFrom(number, count uint64)` as parameter `count`. Due to integer overflow, `UINT64_MAX` value is then passed as the `count` argument to function `GetHeadersFrom(number, count uint64)`. This allows an attacker to bypass `maxHeadersServe` and request all headers from the latest block back to the genesis block. 

##### Patches

The fix has been included in geth version `1.13.15` and onwards. 

The vulnerability was patched in: [https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/29534](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/29534)

##### Workarounds

No workarounds have been made public. 

##### References

No more information is released at this time.

##### Credit

This issue was disclosed responsibly by DongHan Kim via the Ethereum bug bounty program. Thank you for your cooperation. 

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

### [`v1.17.0`](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/releases/tag/v1.17.0): Eezo-Inlaid Circuitry (v1.17.0)

<!-- Eezo-Inlaid Circuitry (v1.17.0) -->

This is a feature release, with all accumulated development from the last 3 months. See below for the highlights.

Note that this release contains multiple critical security fixes, as well as many bug fixes, and is recommended for all users. However, if you are cautious about upgrades, you can also install v1.16.9 which has just the critical security fixes. Specifically, this release fixes [CVE-2026-26313](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/security/advisories/GHSA-689v-6xwf-5jf3), [CVE-2026-26314](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/security/advisories/GHSA-2gjw-fg97-vg3r), [CVE-2026-26315](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/security/advisories/GHSA-m6j8-rg6r-7mv8).

We recommend recreating your p2p node key after installing this update, which you can do by removing the `DATADIR/geth/nodekey` file before restarting geth. Note this will cause a change in the p2p node ID, which may break static peering setups.

##### Highlights

##### Path-based Archive Node with Proofs

The path-based archive node can now serve proofs (via `eth_getProof`) for the state of older blocks.

You can configure the block range that supports proving independently from other archive state availability. Specifically, you can use the `--history.trienode` command-line flag to set the amount of blocks for which tree nodes will be tracked.

This feature is disabled by default. Note that state history cannot easily be recovered once deleted, as it can only be generated by processing blocks. However, you can enable trienode history (and/or state history) at any time to turn a full node into a partial archive node, keeping state from that point in time onwards.

[#​32727](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32727), [#​32621](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32621), [#​33551](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33551), [#​32981](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32981), [#​33399](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33399), [#​32913](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32913), [#​33303](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33303), [#​33584](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33584), [#​33329](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33329), [#​33681](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33681), [#​33103](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33103), [#​33098](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33098), [#​33515](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33515), [#​32247](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32247)

##### EraE History Support

Geth now suports the [EraE](https://redirect.github.com/eth-clients/e2store-format-specs/pull/16) file format, an archival format for post-merge chain history.

[#​32157](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32157), [#​33827](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33827)

##### OpenTelemetry Tracing

OpenTelemetry tracing is now supported by the RPC server, including support for distributed tracing.
We have also added some tracing spans for block processing via the engine API, i.e. `engine_newPayload`.

[#​33599](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33599), [#​33452](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33452), [#​33780](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33780), [#​33521](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33521)

- There is now a `--miner.maxblobs` command-line flag to set a limit on blobs included in built blocks ([#​33129](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33129), [#​33302](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33302))

##### Fork Implementation

- We have implemented engine\_getBlobsV3 ([#​33404](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33404), [#​33444](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33444))
- The engine API now rejects calls with wrong payload version ([#​32754](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32754), [#​33322](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33322))
- blsync has been updated for Fusaka ([#​33349](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33349), [#​33272](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33272), [#​33065](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33065), [#​32674](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32674))
- Some work towards the migration of state to a binary tree has landed, and this replaces the Verkle Tree implementation ([#​33807](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33807), [#​33739](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33739), [#​33694](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33694), [#​32445](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32445), [#​33461](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33461))
- Some access list semantics have been fixed while working on EIP-7928 Block-Level Access Lists ([#​33281](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33281), [#​33637](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33637), [#​33450](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33450))

##### Core

- The crypto/ecies library allowed extraction of the private key used for key derivation via observation of response timing. We recommend rotating the node key after applying this update. ([#​33669](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33669))
- When a missing block is encountered during tx unindexing, Geth will now skip it and move on instead of entering an infinite loop. ([#​33573](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33573))
- Geth now optionally collect and export metrics about the total state size ([#​33254](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33254), [#​33376](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33376), [#​33415](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33415))
- There is a new `OnStateUpdate` hook, which is called after all state of a block has been committed. This gives access to the changeset of the block. ([#​33490](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33490))
- Some minor tracing bugs have been fixed ([#​32919](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32919), [#​33148](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33148), [#​33644](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33644), [#​33214](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33214))
- Various minor issues in the freezer database have also been fixed ([#​33747](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33747), [#​33025](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33025), [#​33203](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33203), [#​33344](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33344))
- The `setHead` operation now unsets the finalized block, in cases where the rolled-back block range extends before it. ([#​33486](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33486))
- The `SignatureValues` method of `types.Signer` now reports an error for invalid signature sizes ([#​33647](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33647))
- Geth prints detailed log messages for 'slow blocks' ([#​33655](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33655), [#​33525](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33525), [#​33442](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33442), [#​32812](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32812), [#​33659](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33659), [#​33532](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33532))
- Pebble configuration has been tweaked for improved performance ([#​33697](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33697), [#​33353](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33353), [#​33315](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33315))
- A rare crash in the log indexer related to reorg handling has been fixed ([#​33810](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33810))
- Internal state diff size accounting has been corrected, so state diffs will now be flushed to the disk store less often ([#​33505](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33505))
- Since the keccak256 hash function variant used by Ethereum no longer has a fast-path in the standard library, we have vendored the keccak implementation back into our repository ([#​33323](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33323))

##### Library

- The RLP library now has a RawList type for dealing with un-decoded lists in a more convenient way ([#​33755](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33755), [#​33834](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33834), [#​33840](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33840), [#​33841](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33841))
- The low-level RLP iterator and uses of it have been improved ([#​33245](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33245), [#​33188](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33188), [#​33820](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33820))
- Clef can now sign blob transactions with cell proofs ([#​32910](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32910))
- Fixed some corner-case bugs in metrics exporting ([#​33749](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33749), [#​33748](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33748))
- The hardware wallet library now supports the Ledger Nano Gen5 and correctly enables EIP-712 signing for all supported versions. ([#​33297](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33297), [#​33113](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33113))
- `SignTextWithPassphrase` now works correctly with all supported hardware wallets ([#​33138](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33138))
- Some minor bugs were fixed in the keystore implementation ([#​33606](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33606), [#​33602](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33602), [#​33090](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33090))
- The `bitutil.XORBytes` function has been deprecated in favor of stdlib package crypto/subtle ([#​33331](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33331))
- A memory leak in the beacon chain light client was fixed ([#​33483](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33483))

##### RPC

- `eth_getTransactionByHash` now returns the `blockTimestamp` as part of the transaction object ([#​33709](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33709))
- Error codes for some conditions in `eth_simulateV1`, `eth_getLogs`, `eth_getStorageAt` have been improved to better comply with the execution RPC spec ([#​33007](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33007), [#​33320](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33320), [#​33282](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33282))
- `eth_simulateV1` now selects the correct set of precompiles for the simulated header ([#​33363](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33363))
- `eth_sendTransaction` and `eth_fillTransaction` now default to EIP-1559 ([#​33058](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33058))
- The GraphQL implementation has received some bug fixes for cases where a resolved item is not found. ([#​33184](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33184), [#​33225](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33225))
- In GraphQL, the `gasPrice` is now retrievable for transaction types 0x3 and 0x4 ([#​33542](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33542))
- The RPC server now enables plain-text HTTP2 for improved performance ([#​33812](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33812))
- The RPC client no longer sends spurious RST\_STREAM HTTP2 frames ([#​33122](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33122))
- Some minor JSON encoding bugs have been fixed in `ethclient` ([#​33693](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33693), [#​33242](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33242), [#​33464](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33464))
- The `gethclient` has a new wrapper of the `callTracer` ([#​31510](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/31510))
- In the `callTracer`, reported logs now contain an `index` field which is the index of the log within the transaction ([#​33629](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33629))

##### P2P Networking

- The transaction pool heartbeat mechanism had some fixes for potential resource leaks ([#​33704](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33704))
- The eth and snap protocol implementations nows validates most p2p messages before decoding their content. This improves security and sync performance in some cases. ([#​33835](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33835))
- The blob transaction pool has seen some bug fixes and now accepts nonce-gapped transactions to a very limited extent ([#​32717](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32717), [#​33775](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33775), [#​33474](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33474), [#​33352](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33352), [#​33301](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33301), [#​33260](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33260))
- Snap sync status is now tracked better, ensuring a snap sync will not be triggered accidentally by the engine API ([#​33157](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33157))
- The snap sync scheduler was improved to better protect the trie database against accidential mutations while the node is processing blocks. This resolves some edge cases where the database could be corrupted ([#​33428](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33428))
- The header sync implementation was fixed to better deal with `setHead` operations during sync ([#​33481](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33481))
- Peer connections delivering stale transactions will be penalized less, since delivery of a few stale transactions is a common occurrence. ([#​32725](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/32725))
- Peers announcing transactions of one type, and delivering a different type, are now disconnected as penalty ([#​33378](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33378))
- Similarly, peers delivering invalid KZG proofs will now be disconnected ([`5b99d2b`](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/commit/5b99d2bba4))
- The transaction pool has new metrics for the number of accounts with transactions ([#​33646](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33646), [#​33654](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33654))

For a full rundown of the changes please consult the Geth [1.17.0](https://redirect.github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/milestone/197?closed=1) release milestone.

### @​babel/core: Arbitrary File Read via sourceMappingURL Comment
[CVE-2026-49356](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-49356) / [GHSA-4x5r-pxfx-6jf8](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-4x5r-pxfx-6jf8)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Using `@babel/core` to compile maliciously crafted code can allow ab attacker to read any source map from the system that is running Babel, if these conditions are _all_ true:
- the attacker controls the input source code
- the attacker can read the output source code
- the attacker knows the path of the source map file that they want to read

**Users that only compile trusted code are not impacted.**

##### Patches

The vulnerability has been fixed in `@babel/core@7.29.6` and `@babel/core@8.0.0-rc.6`.

##### Workarounds

Callers can mitigate the issue without upgrading by setting [`inputSourceMap: false`](https://babeljs.io/docs/options#inputsourcemap) in their Babel options.

Callers can also manually extract the `#sourceMappingURL` comment from the input source code, validate whether the source map that it links to is allowed to be read, and if it is pass an object to `inputSourceMap` (passing `false` when it's not).

##### Credits

Thanks Teodor-Cristian Radoi for reporting the vulnerability.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 3.2 / 10 (Low)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N`

### gnark-crypto allows unchecked memory allocation during vector deserialization
[GHSA-fj2x-735w-74vq](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fj2x-735w-74vq)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The issue has been reported by @​raefko from @​fuzzinglabs. Excerpts from the report:
> A critical vulnerability exists in the gnark-crypto library's `Vector.ReadFrom()` function that allows an attacker to trigger arbitrary memory allocation by crafting malicious input data. An attacker can cause the verifier to attempt allocating up to 128 GB of memory with a minimal malicious input, leading to out-of-memory crashes and denial of service.
> ### **Root Cause**
> 
> 
> The vulnerability stems from **unchecked deserialization** of attacker-controlled length fields in the gnark-crypto library's `Vector.ReadFrom()` function. The function reads a 4-byte unsigned integer from untrusted input and directly uses it to allocate memory without any validation or bounds checking.
> 
> ### **Vulnerable Code Path**
> 
> ```
> User Input (Malicious Proof/Data)
>          ↓
> gnark Proof/Data Deserialization
>          ↓
> Vector.ReadFrom() (ecc/bn254/fr/vector.go:136-144)
>   → sliceLen := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(buf[:4])   // ← ATTACKER-CONTROLLED
>   → (*vector) = make(Vector, sliceLen)             // ← UNCHECKED ALLOCATION
>          ↓
> runtime.makeslice attempts 100+ GB allocation
>          ↓
> fatal error: runtime: out of memory → SIGABRT
> 
> ```
>
> ### **Vulnerable Code**
> 
> **File**: [`gnark-crypto@v0.14.0+/ecc/bn254/fr/vector.go:136-144`](https://redirect.github.com/Consensys/gnark-crypto/blob/8310aae2de6104d3fe3610e3370b2bed10c63111/ecc/bn254/fr/vector.go#L136)
> 
> The code reads a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer (`sliceLen`) directly from the input stream and uses it to allocate a slice without any bounds checking or validation. Each element is 32 bytes (fr.Element for BN254 curve), so an attacker can request up to:
> 
> **Maximum Allocation**: `2^32 elements × 32 bytes = 137,438,953,472 bytes ≈ 128 GB`
> 
> ## **Root Cause Analysis**
> 
> The gnark-crypto library implements a generic serialization format for field element vectors. The format is:
> 
> ```
> [4 bytes: length (n)] [n × 32 bytes: elements]
> ```
> 
> The deserialization code **trusts** the length field implicitly without any validation. This is a classic **integer-to-allocation vulnerability** pattern, similar to issues that have affected many serialization libraries over the years.

##### Impact

The issue impacts users deserializing vectors directly from untrusted sources. In case of malicious input it would lead to OOM in case the server doesn't have sufficient memory (depending on the field, but could allocate from 32GB to 196GB).

##### Patches

The issue is patched in [https://github.com/Consensys/gnark-crypto/pull/759](https://redirect.github.com/Consensys/gnark-crypto/pull/759). It will be backported to gnark-crypto v0.18 and v0.19.

##### Workarounds

The user could manually peek into the first 4 bytes of the serialized data to estimate if the header would allocate large amounts of memory.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

### gRPC-Go: xDS RBAC and HTTP/2 Vulnerabilities
[GHSA-hrxh-6v49-42gf](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-hrxh-6v49-42gf)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
Multiple security vulnerabilities have been identified and addressed in grpc-go affecting the xDS RBAC authorization engine (internal/xds/rbac) and the HTTP/2 transport server implementation (internal/transport). These vulnerabilities could result in:

- Authorization Bypass (Fail-Open) when translating xDS RBAC policies containing `Metadata` or `RequestedServerName` fields.
- Denial of Service (High CPU Consumption) due to an HTTP/2 Rapid Reset mitigation bypass during client-initiated stream resets.
- Denial of Service (Server Panic) when parsing crafted xDS RBAC policies containing `NOT` rules around unsupported fields.

##### Impact
_What kind of vulnerability is it? Who is impacted?_

##### xDS RBAC Authorization Bypass via `Metadata` & `RequestedServerName` matchers

- Affected Component: xDS RBAC 
- Impact: When building policy matchers for gRPC RBAC from xDS configurations, unsupported `permission` and `principal` rules (specifically `Metadata` and `RequestedServerName`) were silently ignored and treated as no-ops.
  - If an authorization policy relied purely on these matchers for access control, treating those rules as no-ops effectively removed the restrictions.
